**Commentary of al-Shawkani (Fath al-Qadir) on Surah 19, verses 27–40 (Part 2 of 2)**

﴿And warn them of the Day of Regret﴾, that is, the Day when they will all feel regret. The evildoer will regret his evil deeds, and the doer of good will regret not having increased his good deeds. ﴿When the matter has been decided﴾, that is, when the reckoning has been completed, the scrolls have been folded up, the people of Paradise are in Paradise, and the people of the Fire are in the Fire. The clause ﴿while they are heedless﴾ is in a place of *naṣb* (accusative case, *maḥall naṣb*, the grammatical position of the Arabic word *naṣb*) as a *ḥāl* (circumstantial clause, describing the state of the subject at the time of the action), meaning: heedless of what is being done to them. Likewise, the clause ﴿and they do not believe﴾ is in a place of *naṣb* as a *ḥāl*.

﴿Indeed, We inherit the earth and whoever is upon it﴾, that is, We cause its inhabitants to die, so that no one remains on it to inherit from the dead. It is as if He, glorified be He, has inherited the earth and whoever is upon it, since He causes them all to die. ﴿And to Us they will be returned﴾, that is, they will be brought back to Us on the Day of Resurrection, and We will recompense each one for his deeds. Something similar has already been mentioned in Surah al-Hijr.

Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim transmitted from Qatadah regarding His words ﴿the word of truth﴾, that he said: "Allah is the Truth, Mighty and Majestic."

ʿAbd al-Razzaq and Ibn Abi Hatim transmitted from him regarding His words ﴿about which they dispute﴾, that he said: "The Children of Israel gathered and brought out from among them four men, one scholar from each group. They disputed about ʿIsa when he was raised. One of them said: 'He is Allah, who descended to the earth, gave life to whomever He gave life to, caused to die whomever He caused to die, and then ascended to the heavens.' These were the Yaʿqubiyyah. The other three said: 'You have lied.' Then two of them said to the third: 'Say about him.' He said: 'He is the son of Allah.' These were the Nestorians. The two said: 'You have lied.' Then one of the two said to the other: 'Say about him.' He said: 'He is the third of three: Allah is a god, ʿIsa is a god, and his mother is a god.' These were the Israelites, who were the kings of the Christians. The fourth said: 'You have lied. He is the servant of Allah, His messenger, His spirit, and His word.' These were the Muslims. Each man had followers according to what he had said, so they fought, and [the Yaʿqubiyyah] prevailed over the Muslims. This is the statement of Allah, glorified be He: ﴿and they kill those who enjoin justice among the people﴾ [Āl ʿImrān: 21]."¹⁰³

Qatadah also said: "They are the ones of whom Allah said: ﴿so the factions differed among themselves﴾." He said: "They disagreed about Him and became factions. The people then argued, and a Muslim man said: 'I ask you by Allah: do you know that ʿIsa used to eat food, and that Allah does not eat?' They said: 'Yes, indeed.' He said: 'Do you know that ʿIsa used to sleep, and that Allah does not sleep?' They said: 'Yes, indeed.' The Muslims defeated them in argument, so the people fought one another. It has been reported to us that the Yaʿqubiyyah prevailed that day, and the Muslims were struck down. Then Allah revealed: ﴿So woe to those who disbelieved, from the scene of a great Day﴾."

Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim transmitted from Ibn ʿAbbas regarding His words ﴿How clearly they will hear and see [on the Day they come to Us]﴾, that he said: "The disbelievers on that Day will hear and see the most of anything, while today they neither hear nor see."

ʿAbd al-Razzaq, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim transmitted from Qatadah regarding His words ﴿the Day they come to Us﴾, that he said: "That is the Day of Resurrection."

al-Bukhari, Muslim, and others transmitted from Abu Saʿid al-Khudri, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "When the people of Paradise enter Paradise and the people of the Fire enter the Fire, Death will be brought in the form of a white-speckled ram. It will be stopped between Paradise and the Fire, and it will be said: 'O people of Paradise, do you recognize this?' They will crane their necks and look at it, and they will say: 'Yes, this is Death,' and all of them have seen it. Then it will call out to the people of the Fire: 'Do you recognize this?' They will crane their necks and look at it, and they will say: 'Yes, this is Death,' and all of them have seen it. Then it will be commanded and slaughtered. And it will be said: 'O people of Paradise, eternity without death! O people of the Fire, eternity without death!'" Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited ﴿And warn them of the Day of Regret﴾, the verse, and he gestured with his hand, and said: "The people of the world are in heedlessness."

al-Nasaʾi, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Ibn Mardawayh transmitted something similar from Abu Hurayrah, traced to the Prophet (ﷺ). Ibn Jarir transmitted through the chain of ʿAli ibn Abi Talhah, from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: "The Day of Regret is one of the names of the Day of Resurrection," and he recited: ﴿lest a soul should say: "Oh, my regret over what I neglected concerning Allah"﴾ [al-Zumar: 56]. But this ʿAli is weak. Moreover, the verse that Ibn ʿAbbas used as evidence does not establish the claimed point either by *muṭābaqa* (direct correspondence of meaning), *taḍammun* (inclusion of part of the meaning), or *iltizām* (necessary implication).

Commentary of al-Shawkani (Fath al-Qadir) on surah 19, verse 27–40 (part 1 of 2):

When Maryam (peace be upon her) was reassured by what she had seen of the signs and had finished her postpartum period, she came to them carrying him, meaning ʿĪsā. The clause "carrying him" (taḥmiluhu) is in the accusative position as a circumstantial clause (ḥāl). Her coming to them was from the distant place to which she had withdrawn. When they saw the child with her, they grieved, and they were a righteous household. They said, denouncing that, ﴿O Maryam, you have certainly come with﴾ i.e., you have done ﴿a strange thing (shayʾan farīyā)﴾. Abu ʿUbayda said: al-farī means the wondrous and rare. Al-Akhfash said the same. Al-farʾ means cutting, as if it is something that breaks the custom, or it is certain to be wondrous and rare. Qutrub said: al-farī means the new (fresh) water-skins, i.e., you have come with a matter that is novel and new, which you were not preceded in. Saʿīd ibn Masʿada said: al-farī means the fabricated, the invented. It is said "farayta" and "afraytu" with the same meaning, and a child born of fornication is like a thing that is fabricated. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿nor shall they bring a slander they have invented between their hands and their feet﴾ [al-Mumtahana: 12]. Mujahid said: al-farī means the great.

﴿O sister of Hārūn﴾. There has been disagreement about the meaning of this brotherhood and about who the Hārūn mentioned is. It was said: he is Hārūn, brother of Mūsā, and the meaning is: how can one who we thought was like Hārūn in worship bring forth such a thing? It was said: Maryam was of the descendants of Hārūn, brother of Mūsā, so she was addressed as "O sister of Hārūn," just as one of the Arabs is addressed as "O brother of the Arabs." It was said: she had a brother from her father whose name was Hārūn. It was said: this Hārūn was a righteous man at that time. It was said: rather, at that time there was a wicked man named Hārūn, so they attributed her to him by way of reproach and rebuke. Ibn Jarir related this without naming its transmitter, and it is weak.

﴿Your father was not a man of evil, nor was your mother a woman of unchastity﴾. This contains a repetition of what preceded of reproach and rebuke, and an alert that immorality is not something that should come from the offspring of the righteous.

﴿So she pointed to him﴾, i.e., to ʿĪsā. She was content with pointing and did not order him to speak because she had vowed to the Most Merciful a fast from speech, as was mentioned before. This is on the assumption that she was at that time within the days of her vow. On the assumption that she had emerged from the days of her vow, it may be said that her restriction to pointing was for the sake of emphasizing the great sign, and that this infant understands the pointing and is able to speak.

﴿They said, "How can we speak to one who is in the cradle, a child?"﴾ This interrogative is for denial and wonder at her pointing to that infant that he should speak to them.

Abu ʿUbayda said: there is superfluous filler in the speech, and the meaning is: how can we speak to a child in the cradle, like the saying of the poet:
"And neighbors of ours who were noble."
Al-Zajjaj said: the better view is that "man" (man) is in the sense of a conditional and a response: whoever is a child in the cradle, how can we speak to him? Ibn al-Anbari preferred this and said: it is not permissible to say that "kāna" is superfluous, since it has put "ṣabiyyan" in the accusative. This can be answered by saying that the one who holds its superfluity makes the verb governing it "nukallimu," as its estimate was given earlier. It was said: "kāna" here is the complete one meaning coming into being and existence, and this was refuted by saying that if it were complete it would not need a predicate. The cradle (mahd) is a well-known thing used for putting a child to sleep.

The meaning is: how can we speak to one whose way is to be put to sleep in the cradle because of his youth? It was said: here it means the mother's lap. It was said: it is a bed like a cradle.

When ʿĪsā heard their speech, ﴿he said, "Indeed, I am the servant of Allah"﴾, so the first thing he uttered was the acknowledgment of servanthood to Him. ﴿He has given me the Scripture (ātānī al-kitāb)﴾, i.e., the Gospel. That is, He decreed for me that I be given the Scripture and prophethood in eternity, even though it had not yet been revealed to him in that state and he had not yet become a prophet. It was said: He gave him the Scripture and made him a prophet in that state, but this is far-fetched.

﴿And He has made me blessed wherever I am﴾, i.e., wherever I may be. Barakah originally derives from the kneeling of the camel (burūk al-baʿīr). The meaning: He made me firm in the religion of Allah. It was said: barakah is increase and elevation, as if he said: He made me in all things increasing, elevated, and successful. It was said: the meaning of mubārak is one who benefits the servants. It was said: one who teaches good. It was said: one who enjoins good and forbids evil. ﴿And He has enjoined upon me prayer (al-ṣalāh)﴾, i.e., commanded me to it, and zakah, the zakah of wealth, or the purification of the soul, ﴿as long as I remain alive﴾, i.e., for the duration of my life. These past-tense verbs are of the type of treating what has not yet occurred as though it had occurred, to alert to the certainty of its occurrence because it had already preceded in the binding decree.

﴿And dutiful to my mother﴾ is coordinated with "blessed." He restricted it to dutifulness to his mother because he knew in that state that he had no father. It is read "wa-birran" with a kasra on the bāʾ, as a verbal noun described by it for emphasis. ﴿And He has not made me a tyrant, wretched﴾. The tyrant (jabbār) is one who magnifies himself and sees no right of anyone over him. The wretched (shaqī) is one who disobeys his Lord, (p-889) and it is said: the disappointed, and it is said: the disobedient to parents.

﴿And peace is upon me the day I was born, and the day I die, and the day I am raised alive﴾. The exegetes said: peace here means safety, i.e., safety upon me the day I was born, so that Satan did not harm me at that time, nor misled me at death nor at resurrection. It was said: what is meant is greeting.

It was said: the lām is for the genus, and it was said: for the specific reference, i.e., that peace directed at Yaḥyā in these three situations is directed at me. It was said: the Messiah did not speak after this statement until he reached the age at which children customarily speak. Saʿīd ibn Manṣūr and Ibn ʿAsākir related from Ibn ʿAbbās regarding His saying: ﴿Then she brought him to her people, carrying him﴾, he said: after forty days, after she had recovered from her postpartum bleeding. Ibn Abi Shayba, Ahmad, ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd, Muslim, al-Tirmidhi, al-Nasa'i and others related from al-Mughira ibn Shuʿba who said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sent me to the people of Najran. They said: Tell us about what you recite: ﴿O sister of Hārūn﴾, while Mūsā was before ʿĪsā by so-and-so many years. He said: I returned and mentioned that to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and he said: Did you not tell them that they used to name themselves after the prophets and the righteous before them?" This prophetic explanation suffices against all that was narrated from the early generations on this matter.

Ibn Abi Hatim related from Anas who said: "ʿĪsā had studied the Gospel and its rulings in his mother's womb, and that is His saying: ﴿Indeed, I am the servant of Allah; He has given me the Scripture﴾." ʿAbd al-Razzaq, Ibn Abi Shayba, ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim related from ʿIkrima regarding His saying: ﴿He has given me the Scripture﴾ the verse, he said: He decreed that I be as such.

Al-Ismaʿili in his Muʿjam, Abu Nuʿaym in al-Hilya, Ibn Mardawayh and Ibn al-Najjar related from Abu Hurayra who said: "The Prophet (ﷺ) said regarding the saying of ʿĪsā ﴿and He has made me blessed wherever I am﴾: He made me a benefactor to people wherever I turn."

Ibn ʿAdi and Ibn ʿAsakir related from Ibn Masʿud from the Prophet (ﷺ) regarding His saying: ﴿and He has made me blessed﴾, he said: a teacher and an educator.

Ibn Abi Hatim related from Ibn ʿAbbas regarding His saying: ﴿and He has not made me a tyrant, wretched﴾: he said: disobedient.

﴿That is ʿĪsā, son of Maryam — the word of truth about which they dispute﴾. ﴿It is not for Allah to take a son; exalted is He. Al-Zajjaj said: "That" which he said, "I am the servant of Allah," is ʿĪsā son of Maryam, not what the Christians say, that he is the son of Allah and that he is a god.

It was said: the estimate is: this speech is the word of truth, and it is of the type of the attribute being attributed to the qualifier, like "ḥaqq al-yaqīn." It will be stopped between Paradise and the Fire, and it will be said: 'O people of Paradise, do you recognize this?' They will crane their necks and look at it, and they will say: 'Yes, this is Death,' and all of them have seen it. Then it will call out to the people of the Fire: 'Do you recognize this?' They will crane their necks and look at it, and they will say: 'Yes, this is Death,' and all of them have seen it. Then it will be commanded and slaughtered. And it will be said: 'O people of Paradise, eternity without death! O people of the Fire, eternity without death!'" Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited ﴿And warn them of the Day of Regret﴾, the verse, and he gestured with his hand, and said: "The people of the world are in heedlessness."

al-Nasaʾi, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Ibn Mardawayh transmitted something similar from Abu Hurayrah, traced to the Prophet (ﷺ). Ibn Jarir transmitted through the chain of ʿAli ibn Abi Talhah, from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: "The Day of Regret is one of the names of the Day of Resurrection," and he recited: ﴿lest a soul should say: "Oh, my regret over what I neglected concerning Allah"﴾ [al-Zumar: 56]. But this ʿAli is weak. Moreover, the verse that Ibn ʿAbbas used as evidence does not establish the claimed point either by *muṭābaqa* (direct correspondence of meaning), *taḍammun* (inclusion of part of the meaning), or *iltizām* (necessary implication).

These are the idols that Azar worshipped. Abraham (peace be upon him) presented to his father the proofs and counsels, and began each of them with the vocative, which carries gentleness and softness, seeking to win his heart and in obedience to the command of his Lord.

Then he repeated his call to the truth, saying: ﴿O my father, indeed there has come to me of knowledge that which has not come to you﴾. He informed him that he had received a share of knowledge that had not reached his father, and that there had newly come to him what would enable him to reach the truth, and be capable through it of guiding the astray. For this reason he commanded him to follow him, saying: ﴿So follow me; I will guide you to a straight path﴾, meaning an even path, leading to the goal and saving from what is disliked.

Then he reinforced this with another counsel that restrains him from what he is engaged in, saying: ﴿O my father, do not worship Satan﴾, meaning do not obey him, for worshipping idols is obedience to Satan. Then he gave the reason in his saying: ﴿Indeed, Satan has ever been, to the Most Merciful, disobedient﴾, when he abandoned what he was commanded regarding prostrating to Adam. Whoever obeys one who is disobedient to Allah, glorified is He, is himself disobedient to Allah, and the disobedient deserves to have blessings stripped from him and vengeance descend upon him.

Al-Kisa'i said: al-'asiyy and al-'asi have the same meaning.

Then he explained to him what prompted these counsels, saying: ﴿O my father, indeed I fear that a punishment from the Most Merciful will touch you﴾. Al-Farra' said: the meaning of "I fear" here is "I know."

Most scholars said: fear here is to be taken in its literal sense, because Abraham was not certain that his father would die in disbelief, for if he had been certain of that he would not have occupied himself with advising him. The meaning of fear for another is that one expects harm to reach that other. ﴿So you would be to Satan a companion﴾, meaning: if you obey Satan, you will be with him in the Fire and the curse, so you will by this cause be an ally, or you will be an ally in punishment with him. There is no true allegiance here, as in His saying, glorified is He: ﴿Intimate friends that Day will be enemies to one another﴾ [Az-Zukhruf: 67]. It was also said that al-walliyy means "the follower," and it was said that it means "the near one," i.e., you would be near to Satan in the Fire.

When these beneficial counsels and acceptable admonitions reached the hearing of Azar, he met them with harshness, roughness and severity, and so said: ﴿Do you reject my gods, O Abraham?﴾ The interrogative is for reproach, rebuke and astonishment. The meaning: are you turning away from them and turning to others? Then he threatened him, saying: ﴿If you do not desist, I will surely stone you﴾, meaning with stones. It was also said: with the tongue, so its meaning would be "I will surely revile you." It was also said: its meaning is "I will surely strike you," and it was said: "I will surely expose your affair." ﴿And leave me alone a long time﴾, meaning for a long period.

Al-Kisa'i said: it is said: "I abandoned him for a long time (maliyyan), and (malwatan) and (mala'atan)," meaning a long period of time, which is lengthy. From it is the saying of Muhalhil:

*So the deaf mountains split at his death, and the widowed women wept over him for a long time.*

It was also said: its meaning is "withdraw from me while your honor is intact, so that no shame from me befalls you." Ibn Jarir chose this view. On this view, (maliyyan) is an accusative of state (hal) from Abraham; and on the first view it is an accusative of time (zarf).

When Abraham saw his father's persistence in obstinacy, ﴿he said: Peace be upon you﴾, meaning a greeting of farewell and parting, like His saying: ﴿And when the ignorant address them, they say: Peace﴾ [Al-Furqan: 63]. It was also said: its meaning is: safety from me to you. This was said by Ibn Jarir. He granted him security despite his disbelief because he had not been commanded to fight him. The first view is preferable, and it is the view of the majority. It was also said: its meaning is a supplication for his safety, seeking to win him and to treat him gently.

Then he promised him that he would ask Allah, glorified is He, for forgiveness for him, in order to win him over and in hope of his softening and the removal of his harshness:

*The old man does not abandon his ways until he is buried in the dust of his grave.*

This promise was made by him before he knew that his father would die in disbelief and the word would be due against him. For this reason Allah, glorified is He, said in another place: ﴿So when it became clear to him that he was an enemy of Allah, he disassociated himself from him﴾ [At-Tawbah: 114], after His saying: ﴿And the request for forgiveness by Abraham for his father was only because of a promise he had made to him﴾ [At-Tawbah: 114].

The clause ﴿Indeed, He has ever been gracious to me﴾ is an explanation of what precedes it. The meaning: I will ask forgiving for you from Allah, for He has always been abundantly kind and gentle to me. It is said: (hafiya bihi) and (tahaffa): when he was kind to him. Al-Kisa'i said: it is said: "He was kind to me (hafiya bi) with great kindness (hafawatan) and (hafwatan)."

Al-Farra' said: ﴿He has ever been gracious to me﴾ means: knowing, gentle, who responds to me when I call upon Him.

Then Khalil (Abraham) explicitly stated what his greeting had implied of farewell and parting, saying: ﴿And I will leave you and what you call upon besides Allah﴾, meaning: I will migrate with my religion away from you and away from your objects of worship, since you did not accept my counsel and my call did not benefit you. ﴿And I will call upon my Lord alone; perhaps I will not be in my supplication to my Lord unfortunate﴾, meaning: disappointed. It was also said: disobedient.

It was said: by this supplication he intended that Allah grant him a son and family with whom he would find companionship in his solitude and to whom he would turn for comfort in his loneliness. It was also said: he intended his supplication for his father's guidance. The word (*'asa*, perhaps) indicates doubt, because he did not know whether it would be granted to him regarding him or not.

The first view is preferable because of His saying: ﴿So when he had left them and what they worshipped besides Allah, We gave him Isaac and Jacob﴾, meaning: We made these bestowed ones a family and offspring in place of the family he had left. ﴿And each We made a prophet﴾, meaning each one of the two. The accusative of (kullan) is because it is the first object of (ja'alna), and it was placed before it for specification, but this is in relation to themselves, not in relation to others than them, meaning: each one of them We made a prophet, not some of them over others.

﴿And We bestowed upon them of Our mercy﴾, by making them prophets. He mentioned this after the explicit statement that they were made prophets, to clarify that prophethood is among the matters of mercy.

It was also said: the intended "mercy" here is wealth. It was said: children. It was said: the Book. It is not far-fetched that all of these matters fall under it. ﴿And We made for them a tongue of truth, exalted﴾. "A tongue of truth" means good praise. It is expressed by "tongue" because it is conveyed through it, just as "hand" is used for gift. Its attribution to truth and its description as exalted indicates that they deserve what is said of them in praise upon the tongues of the servants.

Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim transmitted from Ibn 'Abbas regarding His saying: ﴿I will surely stone you﴾: he said: "I will surely revile you." ﴿And leave me alone a long time﴾: he said: "a period."

Ibn Jarir and Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim transmitted from him: ﴿And leave me alone a long time﴾, he said: "Keep away from me in safety."

Ibn Abi Hatim also transmitted from him, regarding the verse, he said: "Keep away from me unharmed before a punishment from me befalls you."

'Abd ibn Humayd transmitted, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr and 'Ikrimah: ﴿maliyyan﴾ "for a long time."

'Abd al-Razzaq and 'Abd ibn Humayd transmitted, from Qatadah, who said: "unharmed."

'Abd ibn Humayd transmitted, from al-Hasan, the same.

Ibn Abi Hatim transmitted from him regarding His saying: ﴿And We gave him Isaac and Jacob﴾, he said: "He means: We gave him Isaac and Jacob, the son of his son."

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim also transmitted from him regarding His saying: ﴿And We made for them a tongue of truth, exalted﴾, he said: "good praise."

Abraham (peace be upon him) presented to his father the proofs and counsels, and began each of them with the vocative, which carries gentleness and softness, seeking to win his heart and in obedience to the command of his Lord.

Then he repeated his call to the truth, saying: ﴿O my father, indeed there has come to me of knowledge that which has not come to you﴾. He informed him that he had received a share of knowledge that had not reached his father, and that there had newly come to him what would enable him to reach the truth, and be capable through it of guiding the astray. For this reason he commanded him to follow him, saying: ﴿So follow me; I will guide you to a straight path﴾, meaning an even path, leading to the goal and saving from what is disliked.

Then he reinforced this with another counsel that restrains him from what he is engaged in, saying: ﴿O my father, do not worship Satan﴾, meaning do not obey him, for worshipping idols is obedience to Satan. Then he gave the reason in his saying: ﴿Indeed, Satan has ever been, to the Most Merciful, disobedient﴾, when he abandoned what he was commanded regarding prostrating to Adam. Whoever obeys one who is disobedient to Allah, glorified is He, is himself disobedient to Allah, and the disobedient deserves to have blessings stripped from him and vengeance descend upon him.

Al-Kisa'i said: al-'asiyy and al-'asi have the same meaning.

Then he explained to him what prompted these counsels, saying: ﴿O my father, indeed I fear that a punishment from the Most Merciful will touch you﴾. Al-Farra' said: the meaning of "I fear" here is "I know."

Most scholars said: fear here is to be taken in its literal sense, because Abraham was not certain that his father would die in disbelief, for if he had been certain of that he would not have occupied himself with advising him. The meaning of fear for another is that one expects harm to reach that other. ﴿So you would be to Satan a companion﴾, meaning: if you obey Satan, you will be with him in the Fire and the curse, so you will by this cause be an ally, or you will be an ally in punishment with him. There is no true allegiance here, as in His saying, glorified is He: ﴿Intimate friends that Day will be enemies to one another﴾ [Az-Zukhruf: 67]. It was also said that al-walliyy means "the follower," and it was said that it means "the near one," i.e., you would be near to Satan in the Fire.

When these beneficial counsels and acceptable admonitions reached the hearing of Azar, he met them with harshness, roughness and severity, and so said: ﴿Do you reject my gods, O Abraham?﴾ The interrogative is for reproach, rebuke and astonishment. The meaning: are you turning away from them and turning to others? Then he threatened him, saying: ﴿If you do not desist, I will surely stone you﴾, meaning with stones. It was also said: with the tongue, so its meaning would be "I will surely revile you." It was also said: its meaning is "I will surely strike you," and it was said: "I will surely expose your affair." ﴿And leave me alone a long time﴾, meaning for a long period.

Al-Kisa'i said: it is said: "I abandoned him for a long time (maliyyan), and (malwatan) and (mala'atan)," meaning a long period of time, which is lengthy. From it is the saying of Muhalhil:

*So the deaf mountains split at his death, and the widowed women wept over him for a long time.*

It was also said: its meaning is "withdraw from me while your honor is intact, so that no shame from me befalls you." Ibn Jarir chose this view. On this view, (maliyyan) is an accusative of state (hal) from Abraham; and on the first view it is an accusative of time (zarf).

When Abraham saw his father's persistence in obstinacy, ﴿he said: Peace be upon you﴾, meaning a greeting of farewell and parting, like His saying: ﴿And when the ignorant address them, they say: Peace﴾ [Al-Furqan: 63]. It was also said: its meaning is: safety from me to you. This was said by Ibn Jarir. He granted him security despite his disbelief because he had not been commanded to fight him. The first view is preferable, and it is the view of the majority. It was also said: its meaning is a supplication for his safety, seeking to win him and to treat him gently.

Then he promised him that he would ask Allah, glorified is He, for forgiveness for him, in order to win him over and in hope of his softening and the removal of his harshness:

*The old man does not abandon his ways until he is buried in the dust of his grave.*

This promise was made by him before he knew that his father would die in disbelief and the word would be due against him. For this reason Allah, glorified is He, said in another place: ﴿So when it became clear to him that he was an enemy of Allah, he disassociated himself from him﴾ [At-Tawbah: 114], after His saying: ﴿And the request for forgiveness by Abraham for his father was only because of a promise he had made to him﴾ [At-Tawbah: 114].

The clause ﴿Indeed, He has ever been gracious to me﴾ is an explanation of what precedes it. The meaning: I will ask forgiving for you from Allah, for He has always been abundantly kind and gentle to me. It is said: (hafiya bihi) and (tahaffa): when he was kind to him. Al-Kisa'i said: it is said: "He was kind to me (hafiya bi) with great kindness (hafawatan) and (hafwatan)."

Al-Farra' said: ﴿He has ever been gracious to me﴾ means: knowing, gentle, who responds to me when I call upon Him.

Then Khalil (Abraham) explicitly stated what his greeting had implied of farewell and parting, saying: ﴿And I will leave you and what you call upon besides Allah﴾, meaning: I will migrate with my religion away from you and away from your objects of worship, since you did not accept my counsel and my call did not benefit you. ﴿And I will call upon my Lord alone; perhaps I will not be in my supplication to my Lord unfortunate﴾, meaning: disappointed. It was also said: disobedient.

It was said: by this supplication he intended that Allah grant him a son and family with whom he would find companionship in his solitude and to whom he would turn for comfort in his loneliness. It was also said: he intended his supplication for his father's guidance. The word (*'asa*, perhaps) indicates doubt, because he did not know whether it would be granted to him regarding him or not.

The first view is preferable because of His saying: ﴿So when he had left them and what they worshipped besides Allah, We gave him Isaac and Jacob﴾, meaning: We made these bestowed ones a family and offspring in place of the family he had left. ﴿And each We made a prophet﴾, meaning each one of the two. The accusative of (kullan) is because it is the first object of (ja'alna), and it was placed before it for specification, but this is in relation to themselves, not in relation to others than them, meaning: each one of them We made a prophet, not some of them over others.

﴿And We bestowed upon them of Our mercy﴾, by making them prophets. He mentioned this after the explicit statement that they were made prophets, to clarify that prophethood is among the matters of mercy.

It was also said: the intended "mercy" here is wealth. It was said: children. It was said: the Book. It is not far-fetched that all of these matters fall under it. ﴿And We made for them a tongue of truth, exalted﴾. "A tongue of truth" means good praise. It is expressed by "tongue" because it is conveyed through it, just as "hand" is used for gift. Its attribution to truth and its description as exalted indicates that they deserve what is said of them in praise upon the tongues of the servants.

Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim transmitted from Ibn 'Abbas regarding His saying: ﴿I will surely stone you﴾: he said: "I will surely revile you." ﴿And leave me alone a long time﴾: he said: "a period."

Ibn Jarir and Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim transmitted from him: ﴿And leave me alone a long time﴾, he said: "Keep away from me in safety."

Ibn Abi Hatim also transmitted from him, regarding the verse, he said: "Keep away from me unharmed before a punishment from me befalls you."

'Abd ibn Humayd transmitted, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr and 'Ikrimah: ﴿maliyyan﴾ "for a long time."

'Abd al-Razzaq and 'Abd ibn Humayd transmitted, from Qatadah, who said: "unharmed."

'Abd ibn Humayd transmitted, from al-Hasan, the same.

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim transmitted, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿Indeed, He has ever been gracious to me﴾, he said: "kind."

Ibn Abi Hatim transmitted from him regarding His saying: ﴿And We gave him Isaac and Jacob﴾, he said: "He means: We gave him Isaac and Jacob, the son of his son."

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim also transmitted from him regarding His saying: ﴿And We made for them a tongue of truth, exalted﴾, he said: "good praise."

(p-٨٩٢).

God, glory be to Him, followed the story of Ibrahim with the story of Musa, because Musa is next to him in nobility. He placed Musa before Isma'il so that Isma'il would not separate him from the mention of Ya'qub. That is, recite to them from the Qur'an the story of Musa. ﴿Indeed, he was chosen (mukhlasan)﴾. The people of Kufa read the lam with a fatha (mukhlasan, meaning "We made him chosen and purified him"). The rest read it with a kasra (mukhlisan, meaning "he made his worship and monotheism sincerely for Allah, not showing off to the servants"). ﴿And he was a messenger, a prophet﴾. That is, Allah sent him to His servants, and he informed them about Allah through the laws that He had prescribed for them. This is the reason for mentioning "prophet" after "messenger," given that being a messenger entails being a prophet. It seems that by "messenger" he meant its linguistic sense, not its technical sense. And Allah knows best.

Al-Naysaburi said: "The messenger is one who has a scripture from among the prophets, and the prophet is one who reports from Allah, mighty and majestic, even if he does not have a scripture. It would have been appropriate to mention the more general before the more specific, but the requirement of the rhyme (fasila) required the reverse, as in His saying in Ta-Ha: ﴿by the Lord of Harun and Musa﴾ [Ta-Ha: 70]." End of quote.

﴿And We called him from the right side of the mount﴾. That is, We spoke to him from the side of the mount. The mount (al-Tur) is a mountain between Egypt and Madyan, named Zubayr. The meaning of "right" (al-ayman) is that this side was on Musa's right, since the tree was on that side and the call came from it. It does not mean the right side of the mountain itself, for mountains have no right or left. It was also said that the meaning of "al-ayman" is "the blessed," and that the meaning of "the call" is that speech was presented to him from that side. ﴿And We brought him near as a confidant﴾. That is, We drew him close by raising his rank until We spoke to him. The word najiyy (confidant) has the meaning of "one who converses privately," like "companion" or "boon companion." So the drawing near here is a drawing near of honor and esteem. His condition is depicted as the condition of one whom a king brings near for private conversation.

Al-Zajjaj said: "He brought him near in rank, until he heard his private conversation." It was also said: "Allah, glory be to Him, lifted him up until he heard the scratching of the pen." This was narrated from some of the early generation (al-salaf).

﴿And We granted him, out of Our mercy﴾. That is, out of Our blessing. It was also said: "for the sake of Our mercy." Harun is an explanatory appositive (ʿatf bayan), and "a prophet" is a circumstantial qualifier (hal) of him. This was when he asked his Lord, saying: ﴿And appoint for me a minister from my family, Harun, my brother﴾ [Ta-Ha: 29–30].

Allah, glory be to Him, described Isma'il with truthfulness of promise, although all the prophets were like that, because he was famous for it and exceeded in it. Consider that he promised himself patience over being slaughtered and fulfilled that. He would wait for whoever had promised him something for days and nights, until it was said that he waited for one of those who had promised him for a full year.

By "Isma'il" here is meant Isma'il son of Ibrahim. No one disputed this except one whose opinion is not considered, who said: he is Isma'il son of Huzayqil, whom Allah sent to his people. They flayed the skin of his head, so Allah gave him the choice of whatever punishment he wished for them. He asked Him to pardon them and was content with His reward. The verse ﴿and he was a messenger, a prophet﴾ has been cited regarding Isma'il as evidence that a messenger does not have to be the bearer of a sharia, for the children of Ibrahim were upon his sharia. It was also said that He described him with messengerhood because Ibrahim sent him to Jurhum.

﴿And he used to enjoin his family to prayer and zakat﴾. It was said: by "his family" here is meant his community. It was said: Jurhum. It was said: his clan, as in His saying: ﴿And warn your closest kindred﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 214]. By "prayer and zakat" here are meant the two legal acts of worship. It is also permissible that their linguistic meanings are intended. ﴿And he was with his Lord pleasing (mardiyyan)﴾. That is, content (radiyyan), pure, righteous.

Al-Kisa'i and al-Farra' said: whoever says "mardiyy" has formed it from "radītu" (I was pleased). They said: the people of the Hijaz say "mardu."

﴿And mention in the Book Idris﴾. The name of Idris is Akhnukh. It was said he is the grandfather of Nuh, for Nuh is the son of Lamak, son of Matushalakh, son of Akhnukh. On this basis, he would be the grandfather of Nuh's father. This was mentioned by al-Tha'labi and others. It has been said that this is an error, and that Idris is not declined (diptotic) because of being non-Arabic and a proper noun.

He was the first to write with the pen, to look into the stars and calculation, and the first to sew garments. It was said: he was the first of the children of Adam to be given prophethood.

There has been disagreement about the meaning of His saying: ﴿And We raised him to a high station﴾. It was said: Allah raised him to the fourth heaven. It was said: to the sixth. It was said: to the second.

Al-Bukhari narrated in his Sahih from the hadith of the Night Journey (isra'), in which it says: "Among them was Idris in the second." But this is an error in the narration of Sharik ibn ʿAbd Allah ibn Abi Namir.

The correct view is that he was in the fourth heaven, as narrated by Muslim in his Sahih from the hadith of Anas ibn Malik, from the Prophet (ﷺ).

It was also said that what is meant by raising him to a high station is the noble rank of prophethood that he was given. It was said that he was raised to Paradise.

﴿Those are the ones whom Allah has favored among the prophets﴾. The reference is to those mentioned from the beginning of the surah until here. The relative clause is its description. "Among the prophets" is an explanation of the relative. ﴿From the descendants of Adam﴾ is a substitute for it, with the preposition repeated. It was also said that "min" in "from the descendants" of Adam is partitive. ﴿And of those We carried with Nuh﴾. That is, of the descendants of those We carried with him, who are other than Idris, for Ibrahim was of the descendants of Sam son of Nuh. ﴿And of the descendants of Ibrahim﴾, and they are the rest, ﴿and Isra'il﴾. That is, and of the descendants of Isra'il, among whom are Musa, Harun, Yahya, and Isa. It was also said that by His saying: ﴿from the descendants of Adam﴾ He meant Idris alone, and by His saying: ﴿and of those We carried with Nuh﴾ He meant Ibrahim alone, and by His saying: ﴿and of the descendants of Ibrahim﴾ He meant Isma'il, Ishaq, and Ya'qub, and by His saying: ﴿and of the descendants of Ibrahim and Isra'il﴾ He meant Musa, Harun, Zakariyya, Yahya, and Isa. ﴿And of those We guided﴾. That is, among those We guided to Islam ﴿and chose﴾ by faith. ﴿When the verses of the Most Merciful are recited to them, they fall down in prostration and weeping﴾. This is the predicate of "those" (ulā'ika). It is also permissible that the predicate is "those whom Allah has favored." This is a resumptive sentence explaining their humility before Allah and their fear of Him.

The meaning of ﴿fell down in prostration﴾ has already been explained in Surah al-Isra'. It is said: bakā yabkī bukā'an wa bukiyyan (he wept).

Al-Khalil said: when you shorten "bukā'" (weeping) it becomes like "ḥuzn" (sorrow), meaning there is no sound with it. From it is the saying of the poet:

"My eye wept, and rightly so for its weeping, though weeping and wailing profit nothing."

"Sujjadan" (prostrating) is in the accusative as a circumstantial qualifier.

Al-Zajjaj said: Allah has made clear that the prophets, when they heard the verses of Allah, would weep and prostrate. This verse has been cited as evidence for the legislated nature of the prostration of recitation (sujud al-tilawa).

When He praised these prophets with these attributes, to encourage others to follow them and adopt their way, He mentioned their opposites, to deter people from their way. So He said: ﴿Then there succeeded them successors﴾. That is, a bad posterity. The people of language said: a good posterity is called "khalaf" with a fatha on the lam, and a bad posterity is called "khalf" with a sukun on the lam. We have already discussed this at the end of Surah al-A'raf. ﴿who neglected prayer﴾. Most said: the meaning of that is that they delayed it beyond its time. It was said: they wasted the time. It was said: they disbelieved in it and denied its obligation. It was said: they did not perform it in the legislated manner.

The apparent meaning is that whoever delays prayer beyond its time, or abandons one of its obligations, or one of its conditions, or one of its pillars, has neglected it. Included under neglect is whoever abandons it entirely or denies it, by primary inclusion.

They differed about who this verse was revealed concerning. It was said: the Jews. It was said: the Christians. It was said: a people of the community of Muhammad (ﷺ) who will come at the end of time. The meaning of ﴿and followed desires﴾ is that they did what their souls desired and inclined to of the forbidden things, such as drinking wine and fornication. ﴿So they will meet with ghayy﴾. Ghayy, according to the people of language, is evil, just as khayr is guidance (rashad). The meaning is that they will meet with evil, not good. It was said: ghayy is error. It was said: it is loss. It was said: it is the name of a valley in Hell. It was said: there is an omission in the speech, and the implied meaning is: they will meet the recompense of ghayy. So said al-Zajjaj. Similar to this is His saying: ﴿He will meet a penalty (athām)﴾ [al-Furqan: 68], meaning the recompense of a penalty.

﴿Except one who repents and believes and does righteous work﴾. That is, one who repents of what he committed of wasting the prayers and following desires, returns to obedience to Allah, believes in Him, and does righteous work. In this exception there is evidence that the verse is about disbelievers, not Muslims. ﴿Those will enter Paradise﴾. Abu Ja'far, Shayba, Ibn Kathir, Ibn Muhaysin, Abu ʿAmr, Ya'qub, and Abu Bakr read yudkhalūna with a damma on the yā' and a fatha on the khā' (they will be admitted). The rest read it with a fatha on the yā' and a damma on the khā' (they enter). ﴿And they will not be wronged in the least﴾. That is, nothing will be reduced from their rewards, even if it is little, for Allah, glory be to Him, pays them their rewards in full.

The accusative of ﴿gardens of perpetual residence (jannāt ʿadn)﴾ is by substitution for "Paradise," a partial substitution, since the gardens of perpetual residence are a part of Paradise.

Al-Zajjaj said: it is also permissible to read "jannātu ʿadnin" in the nominative, as a beginning (mubtada'). It has been read that way.

Abu Hatim said: were it not for the script, it would be "jannata ʿadnin," meaning the singular in place of the plural. This is nothing, for "Paradise" is a name for the collection of gardens, which are like types with respect to the genus.

It has also been read with the accusative "jannāt" as praise. It has been read "jannata" in the singular.

﴿Which the Most Merciful promised His servants in the unseen﴾. This clause is a qualifier of "jannāt ʿadn." "In the unseen" (bil-ghayb) is in the position of an accusative as a circumstantial qualifier, either of the gardens or of His servants. That is, while they are unseen, or while they are unseen to them. It has been read with "ʿadn" having tanwin (ṣarf) and without it (manʿ), as it is a proper noun for the meaning of ʿadn, which is residence, or a proper noun for the land of Paradise. ﴿Indeed, His promise has always been fulfilled (ma'tiyyan)﴾. That is, what was promised is general, so the gardens enter it by primary inclusion. Al-Farra' said: He did not say ātiyan (coming), because whatever comes to you, you have come to it. Al-Zajjaj said likewise.

﴿They will not hear therein any ill speech﴾. Ill speech (laghw) is idle talk of speech that is discarded and has no benefit. It is a metaphor for their not uttering ill speech. It was said: laghw is everything in which there is no mention of Allah. ﴿Except "Peace"﴾. This is a disconnected exception (istithna' munqati'), meaning the peace of some of them upon others, or the peace of the angels upon them.

Al-Zajjaj said: al-salam is a comprehensive name for good, because it includes safety. The meaning is that the people of Paradise will not hear what pains them, but will only hear what gives them peace. ﴿And for them is their provision therein morning and evening﴾. The commentators said: there is no morning or evening in Paradise, but they are given their provision in proportion to what they know of breakfast and dinner.

﴿That is Paradise which We will give as inheritance to those of Our servants who were mindful of Allah﴾. That is, this is the Paradise whose conditions We have described, which We give as inheritance to those who were among the people of piety, as property remains for the heir after its former owner.

Ya'qub read nūwarrithu with a fatha on the waw and shadda on the rā'. The rest read it with the light form. It was said: there is inversion and displacement in the speech, and the implied meaning is: We give as inheritance to those of Our servants who were mindful of Allah.

Ibn Humayd, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Mujahid, regarding His saying: ﴿And he was a messenger, a prophet﴾, that he said: "The prophet is one who is spoken to and revealed to, but not sent. The wording of Ibn Abi Hatim is: 'The prophets who are not messengers are those to whom revelation is given but who are not sent to anyone. The messengers are the prophets to whom revelation is given and who are sent.'"

ʿAbd al-Razzaq, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Qatada, regarding His saying: ﴿the right side of the mount﴾, that he said: "the right side of the mountain." ﴿And We brought him near as a confidant﴾. He said: "He was saved by his truthfulness."

ʿAbd ibn Humayd narrated from Abu al-ʿAliya, who said: "He brought him near until he heard the scratching of the pen." Something similar was narrated from a group of the Successors (tabi'un).

Al-Firyabi, Ibn Abi Shayba, ʿAbd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and al-Hakim, who authenticated it, narrated from Ibn ʿAbbas regarding the verse that he said: "Until he heard the scratching of the pen writing on the Preserved Tablet." Al-Daylami narrated it from him as a raised (marfu') report.

Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words ﴿And We gave him, out of Our mercy, his brother Harun﴾, that he said: Harun was older than Musa, but He only granted him prophethood.

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words ﴿And We raised him to a lofty station﴾, that he said: Idris was a tailor. He would not make a single stitch without saying, "Glory be to Allah." When evening came, there was no one on earth with better deeds than him. An angel asked his Lord for permission, saying, "My Lord, permit me to descend to Idris." He was permitted, so he came to Idris and said, "I have come to serve you." Idris said, "How can you serve me when you are an angel and I am a human?" Then Idris said, "Is there any relationship between you and the Angel of Death?" The angel said, "He is my brother among the angels." Idris said, "Can you benefit me?" The angel said, "He cannot delay or advance anything, but I will speak to him on your behalf, so that he will be gentle with you at death." Then the angel said, "Ride between my wings." Idris rode, and he ascended to the highest heaven, where he met the Angel of Death while Idris was between the angel's wings. The angel said to him, "I have a need concerning you." He replied, "I know your need. You want to speak to me about Idris. His name has been erased from the register, and only half a blink of an eye remains of his term." Idris died between the wings of the angel.

Ibn Abi Shayba in al-Masahif and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Ibn Abbas that he said: I asked Ka'b, and he related something similar. This is among the Isra'iliyyat (narratives of Israelite origin) that Ka'b transmits.

Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Ibn Abbas that he said: Idris was raised to the sixth heaven.

Al-Tirmidhi, who graded it sound, and Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Mardawayh narrated: Anas ibn Malik narrated to us from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "When I was taken up on the Night Journey, I saw Idris in the fourth heaven."

Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, traced to the Prophet (ﷺ), something similar.

Ibn Abi Shayba, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Mujahid, regarding the verse, that he said: Idris was raised as Isa was raised, and he did not die.

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Ibn Mas'ud that he said: Idris is Ilyas. Al-Suyuti graded it as fair (hasan).

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from al-Suddi, regarding His words ﴿Those are the ones upon whom Allah bestowed favor﴾ to the end, that he said: These are the names of the prophets He mentioned. From the offspring of Adam: Idris and Nuh. Of those carried with Nuh: Ibrahim. From the offspring of Ibrahim: Isma'il, Ishaq and Ya'qub. From the offspring of Isra'il: Musa, Harun, Zakariyya, Yahya and Isa.

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from al-Suddi, regarding His words ﴿Then there succeeded them a succession﴾, that he said: They are the Jews and the Christians.

Abd ibn Humayd narrated from Mujahid, regarding the verse, that he said: They are from this Ummah. They ride upon the roads as cattle ride, not ashamed before people, and not fearing Allah in the sky.

Abd ibn Humayd narrated from Ibn Mas'ud, regarding His words ﴿They neglected the prayer﴾, that he said: Neglecting it does not mean abandoning it. A person may neglect a thing without abandoning it. Rather, neglecting it means not performing it at its time.

Ahmad, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Hibban, al-Hakim, who graded it sound, Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Bayhaqi in Shu'ab al-Iman narrated from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri: "I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recite this verse: ﴿Then there succeeded them a succession who neglected the prayer and followed desires﴾ to the end," and he said: "There will come after sixty years a succession who neglect the prayer and follow desires, ﴿so they will meet error (ghayy)﴾. Then there will come a succession who recite the Qur'an without it passing beyond their throats. The Qur'an will be recited by three: a believer, a hypocrite, and a wicked person."

Ahmad and al-Hakim, who graded it sound, narrated from Uqba ibn Amir: "I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: 'Among my Ummah will be destroyed the People of the Book and the People of Milk.' I said, 'O Messenger of Allah, who are the People of the Book?' He said, 'A people who learn the Book and argue with it against those who believe.' I said, 'Who are the People of Milk?' He said, 'A people who follow desires and neglect the prayers.'"

Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Mardawayh and al-Hakim, who graded it sound, narrated from Aisha that she used to send charity to the people entitled to it and say: "Do not give from it to a Berber man or a Berber woman, for I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: 'They are the successors (khalf) of whom Allah said: ﴿Then there succeeded them a succession﴾.'"

Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words ﴿They will meet ghayy﴾, that he said: loss.

Al-Firyabi, Sa'id ibn Mansur, Hannad, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Tabarani, al-Hakim, who graded it sound, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Ba'th narrated through several chains from Ibn Mas'ud, regarding His words ﴿They will meet ghayy﴾, that he said: Ghayy is a river or a valley in Jahannam, of pus, deep in its bottom and foul in taste, into which those who follow desires will be thrown.

Al-Bara' ibn Azib said that it is a valley in Jahannam, and Ibn al-Mundhir and al-Tabarani narrated this from him. Ibn Jarir, al-Tabarani, Ibn Mardawayh and al-Bayhaqi narrated from Abu Umama, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Even if a rock weighing ten awqiyah were thrown from the edge of Jahannam, it would not reach its bottom in seventy autumns. Then it would reach ghayy and athām." I said, "What are ghayy and athām?" He said: "Two rivers at the bottom of Jahannam, in which flows the pus of the people of the Fire. They are the two that Allah mentioned in His Book: ﴿They will meet ghayy﴾ and ﴿Whoever does that will meet athām﴾ [al-Furqan: 68]."

Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Ibn Abbas, from the Prophet (ﷺ), that he said: "Ghayy is a valley in Jahannam."

Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from him, regarding His words ﴿They will hear therein no vain speech﴾, that he said: falsehood.

Sa'id ibn Mansur, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from him also, regarding His words ﴿Morning and evening﴾, that he said: They will be brought it in the Hereafter in the same measure as they were brought it in this world.

Al-Hakim al-Tirmidhi in Nawadir al-Usul narrated through the route of Aban, from al-Hasan and Abu Qilaba, who both said: "A man said: 'O Messenger of Allah, is there night in Paradise?' He said: 'What has prompted you to this?' He said: 'I heard Allah mention in the Book: ﴿And they will have their provision therein morning and evening﴾. So I said: night is part of morning and evening.' The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'There is no night there. Rather, there is light and radiance, the morning returns upon the afternoon and the afternoon upon the morning. Gifts from Allah come to them at the times of the prayers they used to perform in the world, and the angels greet them.'"

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Abu Hurayra, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "There is no morning among the mornings of Paradise, and all of Paradise is mornings, except that there will be brought to the friend of Allah therein a wife from the Houris with large eyes, and the nearest of them is the one created from saffron." After narrating it, he said: Abu Muhammad said: This is a munkar (rejected) hadith.

(p-٨٩٢).

God, glory be to Him, followed the story of Ibrahim with the story of Musa, because Musa is next to him in nobility. He placed Musa before Isma'il so that Isma'il would not separate him from the mention of Ya'qub. That is, recite to them from the Qur'an the story of Musa. ﴿Indeed, he was chosen (mukhlasan)﴾. The people of Kufa read the lam with a fatha (mukhlasan, meaning "We made him chosen and purified him"). The rest read it with a kasra (mukhlisan, meaning "he made his worship and monotheism sincerely for Allah, not showing off to the servants"). ﴿And he was a messenger, a prophet﴾. That is, Allah sent him to His servants, and he informed them about Allah through the laws that He had prescribed for them. This is the reason for mentioning "prophet" after "messenger," given that being a messenger entails being a prophet. It seems that by "messenger" he meant its linguistic sense, not its technical sense. And Allah knows best.

Al-Naysaburi said: "The messenger is one who has a scripture from among the prophets, and the prophet is one who reports from Allah, mighty and majestic, even if he does not have a scripture. It would have been appropriate to mention the more general before the more specific, but the requirement of the rhyme (fasila) required the reverse, as in His saying in Ta-Ha: ﴿by the Lord of Harun and Musa﴾ [Ta-Ha: 70]." End of quote.

﴿And We called him from the right side of the mount﴾. That is, We spoke to him from the side of the mount. The mount (al-Tur) is a mountain between Egypt and Madyan, named Zubayr. The meaning of "right" (al-ayman) is that this side was on Musa's right, since the tree was on that side and the call came from it. It does not mean the right side of the mountain itself, for mountains have no right or left. It was also said that the meaning of "al-ayman" is "the blessed," and that the meaning of "the call" is that speech was presented to him from that side. ﴿And We brought him near as a confidant﴾. That is, We drew him close by raising his rank until We spoke to him. The word najiyy (confidant) has the meaning of "one who converses privately," like "companion" or "boon companion." So the drawing near here is a drawing near of honor and esteem. His condition is depicted as the condition of one whom a king brings near for private conversation.

Al-Zajjaj said: "He brought him near in rank, until he heard his private conversation." It was also said: "Allah, glory be to Him, lifted him up until he heard the scratching of the pen." This was narrated from some of the early generation (al-salaf).

﴿And We granted him, out of Our mercy﴾. That is, out of Our blessing. It was also said: "for the sake of Our mercy." Harun is an explanatory appositive (ʿatf bayan), and "a prophet" is a circumstantial qualifier (hal) of him. This was when he asked his Lord, saying: ﴿And appoint for me a minister from my family, Harun, my brother﴾ [Ta-Ha: 29–30].

Allah, glory be to Him, described Isma'il with truthfulness of promise, although all the prophets were like that, because he was famous for it and exceeded in it. Consider that he promised himself patience over being slaughtered and fulfilled that. He would wait for whoever had promised him something for days and nights, until it was said that he waited for one of those who had promised him for a full year.

By "Isma'il" here is meant Isma'il son of Ibrahim. No one disputed this except one whose opinion is not considered, who said: he is Isma'il son of Huzayqil, whom Allah sent to his people. They flayed the skin of his head, so Allah gave him the choice of whatever punishment he wished for them. He asked Him to pardon them and was content with His reward. The verse ﴿and he was a messenger, a prophet﴾ has been cited regarding Isma'il as evidence that a messenger does not have to be the bearer of a sharia, for the children of Ibrahim were upon his sharia. It was also said that He described him with messengerhood because Ibrahim sent him to Jurhum.

﴿And he used to enjoin his family to prayer and zakat﴾. It was said: by "his family" here is meant his community. It was said: Jurhum. It was said: his clan, as in His saying: ﴿And warn your closest kindred﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 214]. By "prayer and zakat" here are meant the two legal acts of worship. It is also permissible that their linguistic meanings are intended. ﴿And he was with his Lord pleasing (mardiyyan)﴾. That is, content (radiyyan), pure, righteous.

Al-Kisa'i and al-Farra' said: whoever says "mardiyy" has formed it from "radītu" (I was pleased). They said: the people of the Hijaz say "mardu."

﴿And mention in the Book Idris﴾. The name of Idris is Akhnukh. It was said he is the grandfather of Nuh, for Nuh is the son of Lamak, son of Matushalakh, son of Akhnukh. On this basis, he would be the grandfather of Nuh's father. This was mentioned by al-Tha'labi and others. It has been said that this is an error, and that Idris is not declined (diptotic) because of being non-Arabic and a proper noun.

He was the first to write with the pen, to look into the stars and calculation, and the first to sew garments. It was said: he was the first of the children of Adam to be given prophethood.

There has been disagreement about the meaning of His saying: ﴿And We raised him to a high station﴾. It was said: Allah raised him to the fourth heaven. It was said: to the sixth. It was said: to the second.

Al-Bukhari narrated in his Sahih from the hadith of the Night Journey (isra'), in which it says: "Among them was Idris in the second." But this is an error in the narration of Sharik ibn ʿAbd Allah ibn Abi Namir.

The correct view is that he was in the fourth heaven, as narrated by Muslim in his Sahih from the hadith of Anas ibn Malik, from the Prophet (ﷺ).

It was also said that what is meant by raising him to a high station is the noble rank of prophethood that he was given. It was said that he was raised to Paradise.

﴿Those are the ones whom Allah has favored among the prophets﴾. The reference is to those mentioned from the beginning of the surah until here. The relative clause is its description. "Among the prophets" is an explanation of the relative. ﴿From the descendants of Adam﴾ is a substitute for it, with the preposition repeated. It was also said that "min" in "from the descendants" of Adam is partitive. ﴿And of those We carried with Nuh﴾. That is, of the descendants of those We carried with him, who are other than Idris, for Ibrahim was of the descendants of Sam son of Nuh. ﴿And of the descendants of Ibrahim﴾, and they are the rest, ﴿and Isra'il﴾. That is, and of the descendants of Isra'il, among whom are Musa, Harun, Yahya, and Isa. It was also said that by His saying: ﴿from the descendants of Adam﴾ He meant Idris alone, and by His saying: ﴿and of those We carried with Nuh﴾ He meant Ibrahim alone, and by His saying: ﴿and of the descendants of Ibrahim﴾ He meant Isma'il, Ishaq, and Ya'qub, and by His saying: ﴿and of the descendants of Ibrahim and Isra'il﴾ He meant Musa, Harun, Zakariyya, Yahya, and Isa. ﴿And of those We guided﴾. That is, among those We guided to Islam ﴿and chose﴾ by faith. ﴿When the verses of the Most Merciful are recited to them, they fall down in prostration and weeping﴾. This is the predicate of "those" (ulā'ika). It is also permissible that the predicate is "those whom Allah has favored." This is a resumptive sentence explaining their humility before Allah and their fear of Him.

The meaning of ﴿fell down in prostration﴾ has already been explained in Surah al-Isra'. It is said: bakā yabkī bukā'an wa bukiyyan (he wept).

Al-Khalil said: when you shorten "bukā'" (weeping) it becomes like "ḥuzn" (sorrow), meaning there is no sound with it. From it is the saying of the poet:

"My eye wept, and rightly so for its weeping, though weeping and wailing profit nothing."

"Sujjadan" (prostrating) is in the accusative as a circumstantial qualifier.

Al-Zajjaj said: Allah has made clear that the prophets, when they heard the verses of Allah, would weep and prostrate. This verse has been cited as evidence for the legislated nature of the prostration of recitation (sujud al-tilawa).

When He praised these prophets with these attributes, to encourage others to follow them and adopt their way, He mentioned their opposites, to deter people from their way. So He said: ﴿Then there succeeded them successors﴾. That is, a bad posterity. The people of language said: a good posterity is called "khalaf" with a fatha on the lam, and a bad posterity is called "khalf" with a sukun on the lam. We have already discussed this at the end of Surah al-A'raf. ﴿who neglected prayer﴾. Most said: the meaning of that is that they delayed it beyond its time. It was said: they wasted the time. It was said: they disbelieved in it and denied its obligation. It was said: they did not perform it in the legislated manner.

The apparent meaning is that whoever delays prayer beyond its time, or abandons one of its obligations, or one of its conditions, or one of its pillars, has neglected it. Included under neglect is whoever abandons it entirely or denies it, by primary inclusion.

They differed about who this verse was revealed concerning. It was said: the Jews. It was said: the Christians. It was said: a people of the community of Muhammad (ﷺ) who will come at the end of time. The meaning of ﴿and followed desires﴾ is that they did what their souls desired and inclined to of the forbidden things, such as drinking wine and fornication. ﴿So they will meet with ghayy﴾. Ghayy, according to the people of language, is evil, just as khayr is guidance (rashad). The meaning is that they will meet with evil, not good. It was said: ghayy is error. It was said: it is loss. It was said: it is the name of a valley in Hell. It was said: there is an omission in the speech, and the implied meaning is: they will meet the recompense of ghayy. So said al-Zajjaj. Similar to this is His saying: ﴿He will meet a penalty (athām)﴾ [al-Furqan: 68], meaning the recompense of a penalty.

﴿Except one who repents and believes and does righteous work﴾. That is, one who repents of what he committed of wasting the prayers and following desires, returns to obedience to Allah, believes in Him, and does righteous work. In this exception there is evidence that the verse is about disbelievers, not Muslims. ﴿Those will enter Paradise﴾. Abu Ja'far, Shayba, Ibn Kathir, Ibn Muhaysin, Abu ʿAmr, Ya'qub, and Abu Bakr read yudkhalūna with a damma on the yā' and a fatha on the khā' (they will be admitted). The rest read it with a fatha on the yā' and a damma on the khā' (they enter). ﴿And they will not be wronged in the least﴾. That is, nothing will be reduced from their rewards, even if it is little, for Allah, glory be to Him, pays them their rewards in full.

The accusative of ﴿gardens of perpetual residence (jannāt ʿadn)﴾ is by substitution for "Paradise," a partial substitution, since the gardens of perpetual residence are a part of Paradise.

Al-Zajjaj said: it is also permissible to read "jannātu ʿadnin" in the nominative, as a beginning (mubtada'). It has been read that way.

Abu Hatim said: were it not for the script, it would be "jannata ʿadnin," meaning the singular in place of the plural. This is nothing, for "Paradise" is a name for the collection of gardens, which are like types with respect to the genus.

It has also been read with the accusative "jannāt" as praise. It has been read "jannata" in the singular.

﴿Which the Most Merciful promised His servants in the unseen﴾. This clause is a qualifier of "jannāt ʿadn." "In the unseen" (bil-ghayb) is in the position of an accusative as a circumstantial qualifier, either of the gardens or of His servants. That is, while they are unseen, or while they are unseen to them. It has been read with "ʿadn" having tanwin (ṣarf) and without it (manʿ), as it is a proper noun for the meaning of ʿadn, which is residence, or a proper noun for the land of Paradise. ﴿Indeed, His promise has always been fulfilled (ma'tiyyan)﴾. That is, what was promised is general, so the gardens enter it by primary inclusion. Al-Farra' said: He did not say ātiyan (coming), because whatever comes to you, you have come to it. Al-Zajjaj said likewise.

﴿They will not hear therein any ill speech﴾. Ill speech (laghw) is idle talk of speech that is discarded and has no benefit. It is a metaphor for their not uttering ill speech. It was said: laghw is everything in which there is no mention of Allah. ﴿Except "Peace"﴾. This is a disconnected exception (istithna' munqati'), meaning the peace of some of them upon others, or the peace of the angels upon them.

Al-Zajjaj said: al-salam is a comprehensive name for good, because it includes safety. The meaning is that the people of Paradise will not hear what pains them, but will only hear what gives them peace. ﴿And for them is their provision therein morning and evening﴾. The commentators said: there is no morning or evening in Paradise, but they are given their provision in proportion to what they know of breakfast and dinner.

﴿That is Paradise which We will give as inheritance to those of Our servants who were mindful of Allah﴾. That is, this is the Paradise whose conditions We have described, which We give as inheritance to those who were among the people of piety, as property remains for the heir after its former owner.

Ya'qub read nūwarrithu with a fatha on the waw and shadda on the rā'. The rest read it with the light form. It was said: there is inversion and displacement in the speech, and the implied meaning is: We give as inheritance to those of Our servants who were mindful of Allah.

Ibn Humayd, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Mujahid, regarding His saying: ﴿And he was a messenger, a prophet﴾, that he said: "The prophet is one who is spoken to and revealed to, but not sent. The wording of Ibn Abi Hatim is: 'The prophets who are not messengers are those to whom revelation is given but who are not sent to anyone. The messengers are the prophets to whom revelation is given and who are sent.'"

ʿAbd al-Razzaq, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Qatada, regarding His saying: ﴿the right side of the mount﴾, that he said: "the right side of the mountain." ﴿And We brought him near as a confidant﴾. He said: "He was saved by his truthfulness."

ʿAbd ibn Humayd narrated from Abu al-ʿAliya, who said: "He brought him near until he heard the scratching of the pen." Something similar was narrated from a group of the Successors (tabi'un).

Al-Firyabi, Ibn Abi Shayba, ʿAbd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and al-Hakim, who authenticated it, narrated from Ibn ʿAbbas regarding the verse that he said: "Until he heard the scratching of the pen writing on the Preserved Tablet." Al-Daylami narrated it from him as a raised (marfu') report.

Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words ﴿And We gave him, out of Our mercy, his brother Harun﴾, that he said: Harun was older than Musa, but He only granted him prophethood.

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words ﴿And We raised him to a lofty station﴾, that he said: Idris was a tailor. He would not make a single stitch without saying, "Glory be to Allah." When evening came, there was no one on earth with better deeds than him. An angel asked his Lord for permission, saying, "My Lord, permit me to descend to Idris." He was permitted, so he came to Idris and said, "I have come to serve you." Idris said, "How can you serve me when you are an angel and I am a human?" Then Idris said, "Is there any relationship between you and the Angel of Death?" The angel said, "He is my brother among the angels." Idris said, "Can you benefit me?" The angel said, "He cannot delay or advance anything, but I will speak to him on your behalf, so that he will be gentle with you at death." Then the angel said, "Ride between my wings." Idris rode, and he ascended to the highest heaven, where he met the Angel of Death while Idris was between the angel's wings. The angel said to him, "I have a need concerning you." He replied, "I know your need. You want to speak to me about Idris. His name has been erased from the register, and only half a blink of an eye remains of his term." Idris died between the wings of the angel.

Ibn Abi Shayba in al-Masahif and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Ibn Abbas that he said: I asked Ka'b, and he related something similar. This is among the Isra'iliyyat (narratives of Israelite origin) that Ka'b transmits.

Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Ibn Abbas that he said: Idris was raised to the sixth heaven.

Al-Tirmidhi, who graded it sound, and Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Mardawayh narrated: Anas ibn Malik narrated to us from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "When I was taken up on the Night Journey, I saw Idris in the fourth heaven."

Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, traced to the Prophet (ﷺ), something similar.

Ibn Abi Shayba, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Mujahid, regarding the verse, that he said: Idris was raised as Isa was raised, and he did not die.

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Ibn Mas'ud that he said: Idris is Ilyas. Al-Suyuti graded it as fair (hasan).

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from al-Suddi, regarding His words ﴿Those are the ones upon whom Allah bestowed favor﴾ to the end, that he said: These are the names of the prophets He mentioned. From the offspring of Adam: Idris and Nuh. Of those carried with Nuh: Ibrahim. From the offspring of Ibrahim: Isma'il, Ishaq and Ya'qub. From the offspring of Isra'il: Musa, Harun, Zakariyya, Yahya and Isa.

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from al-Suddi, regarding His words ﴿Then there succeeded them a succession﴾, that he said: They are the Jews and the Christians.

Abd ibn Humayd narrated from Mujahid, regarding the verse, that he said: They are from this Ummah. They ride upon the roads as cattle ride, not ashamed before people, and not fearing Allah in the sky.

Abd ibn Humayd narrated from Ibn Mas'ud, regarding His words ﴿They neglected the prayer﴾, that he said: Neglecting it does not mean abandoning it. A person may neglect a thing without abandoning it. Rather, neglecting it means not performing it at its time.

Ahmad, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Hibban, al-Hakim, who graded it sound, Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Bayhaqi in Shu'ab al-Iman narrated from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri: "I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recite this verse: ﴿Then there succeeded them a succession who neglected the prayer and followed desires﴾ to the end," and he said: "There will come after sixty years a succession who neglect the prayer and follow desires, ﴿so they will meet error (ghayy)﴾. Then there will come a succession who recite the Qur'an without it passing beyond their throats. The Qur'an will be recited by three: a believer, a hypocrite, and a wicked person."

Ahmad and al-Hakim, who graded it sound, narrated from Uqba ibn Amir: "I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: 'Among my Ummah will be destroyed the People of the Book and the People of Milk.' I said, 'O Messenger of Allah, who are the People of the Book?' He said, 'A people who learn the Book and argue with it against those who believe.' I said, 'Who are the People of Milk?' He said, 'A people who follow desires and neglect the prayers.'"

Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Mardawayh and al-Hakim, who graded it sound, narrated from Aisha that she used to send charity to the people entitled to it and say: "Do not give from it to a Berber man or a Berber woman, for I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: 'They are the successors (khalf) of whom Allah said: ﴿Then there succeeded them a succession﴾.'"

Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words ﴿They will meet ghayy﴾, that he said: loss.

Al-Firyabi, Sa'id ibn Mansur, Hannad, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Tabarani, al-Hakim, who graded it sound, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Ba'th narrated through several chains from Ibn Mas'ud, regarding His words ﴿They will meet ghayy﴾, that he said: Ghayy is a river or a valley in Jahannam, of pus, deep in its bottom and foul in taste, into which those who follow desires will be thrown.

Al-Bara' ibn Azib said that it is a valley in Jahannam, and Ibn al-Mundhir and al-Tabarani narrated this from him. Ibn Jarir, al-Tabarani, Ibn Mardawayh and al-Bayhaqi narrated from Abu Umama, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Even if a rock weighing ten awqiyah were thrown from the edge of Jahannam, it would not reach its bottom in seventy autumns. Then it would reach ghayy and athām." I said, "What are ghayy and athām?" He said: "Two rivers at the bottom of Jahannam, in which flows the pus of the people of the Fire. They are the two that Allah mentioned in His Book: ﴿They will meet ghayy﴾ and ﴿Whoever does that will meet athām﴾ [al-Furqan: 68]."

Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Ibn Abbas, from the Prophet (ﷺ), that he said: "Ghayy is a valley in Jahannam."

Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from him, regarding His words ﴿They will hear therein no vain speech﴾, that he said: falsehood.

Sa'id ibn Mansur, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from him also, regarding His words ﴿Morning and evening﴾, that he said: They will be brought it in the Hereafter in the same measure as they were brought it in this world.

Al-Hakim al-Tirmidhi in Nawadir al-Usul narrated through the route of Aban, from al-Hasan and Abu Qilaba, who both said: "A man said: 'O Messenger of Allah, is there night in Paradise?' He said: 'What has prompted you to this?' He said: 'I heard Allah mention in the Book: ﴿And they will have their provision therein morning and evening﴾. So I said: night is part of morning and evening.' The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'There is no night there. Rather, there is light and radiance, the morning returns upon the afternoon and the afternoon upon the morning. Gifts from Allah come to them at the times of the prayers they used to perform in the world, and the angels greet them.'"

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Abu Hurayra, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "There is no morning among the mornings of Paradise, and all of Paradise is mornings, except that there will be brought to the friend of Allah therein a wife from the Houris with large eyes, and the nearest of them is the one created from saffron." After narrating it, he said: Abu Muhammad said: This is a munkar (rejected) hadith.

(p-٨٩٢).

God, glory be to Him, followed the story of Ibrahim with the story of Musa, because Musa is next to him in nobility. He placed Musa before Isma'il so that Isma'il would not separate him from the mention of Ya'qub. That is, recite to them from the Qur'an the story of Musa. ﴿Indeed, he was chosen (mukhlasan)﴾. The people of Kufa read the lam with a fatha (mukhlasan, meaning "We made him chosen and purified him"). The rest read it with a kasra (mukhlisan, meaning "he made his worship and monotheism sincerely for Allah, not showing off to the servants"). ﴿And he was a messenger, a prophet﴾. That is, Allah sent him to His servants, and he informed them about Allah through the laws that He had prescribed for them. This is the reason for mentioning "prophet" after "messenger," given that being a messenger entails being a prophet. It seems that by "messenger" he meant its linguistic sense, not its technical sense. And Allah knows best.

Al-Naysaburi said: "The messenger is one who has a scripture from among the prophets, and the prophet is one who reports from Allah, mighty and majestic, even if he does not have a scripture. It would have been appropriate to mention the more general before the more specific, but the requirement of the rhyme (fasila) required the reverse, as in His saying in Ta-Ha: ﴿by the Lord of Harun and Musa﴾ [Ta-Ha: 70]." End of quote.

﴿And We called him from the right side of the mount﴾. That is, We spoke to him from the side of the mount. The mount (al-Tur) is a mountain between Egypt and Madyan, named Zubayr.
